mdl0End1 refers to one of the end equipment in the Mdl0GeomConnGroup.Mdl0GeomConnGroup has two ends. Each end refers to one of the end equipment in that routing. For instance, one end can be a pump and other end could be a tank. mdl0End1 refers to one of them.NULLs are allowed for this property. If the value is NULL, it can affect validation and split use cases on the connection (Mdl0GeomConnGroup). For details on how validation and split use cases are affected see validateGeomConnGroups and splitGeomConnGroups operations in GeometricConnectivity SOA service.

mdl0End2 refers to one of the end equipment in Mdl0GeomConnGroup.Mdl0GeomConnGroup has two ends. Each end refers to one of the end equipment in that routing. For instance, one end can be a pump and other end could be a tank. mdl0End2 refers to one of them. If mdl0End1 is refers the pump, mdl0End2 refers tank and vice versa.NULLs are allowed for this property. mdl0LogicalId refers to the 2D logical representation of the routing. mdl0LogicalId cannot be null since each connection (Mdl0GeomConnGroup) is basically realizing a 2D logical representation of piping and instrumentation.The 2D logical representation of a routing can have one or more connection (Mdl0GeomConnGroup) objects. An integer value that specifies number of elements to be returned in each search iteration (not used currently).

TcRuntimeType.description: Mdl0SearchDef is the root business object for search recipe and it contains a type attribute that conveniently specifies the type of the inherited expression. An instance of the Mdl0SearchDef object itself represents an Empty Search Expression.Mdl0SearchDef is created to process the search operation and destroyed when the search is finished/stopped.The Mdl0SearchDef may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0SearchDef is used by RDV and 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: An integer value that specify the Search Type. Valid values are -0 (EmptySearch), 1(ResultType), 2 (SelectedContent), 3 (Group), 4 (SavedQuery), 5 (Proximity), 6 (BoxZone), 7 (PlaneZone), 8 (PartitionSearch), 9 (Closure), 10 (UnassignedPartition), 11 (OptionSet)
A Boolean value that specify if the true shape analysis is required on the search expression.
The business object type of the objects to be returned as an output of the search. All objects returned will be of, or sub-type of this type

The key identifies which root or member object the predicate applies to. E.g. value "Bom0Part" identifies that predicate test is to be applied against a data of type Bom0Part. Traversal adaptor performs the required database query JOINs to traverse from type identified by mdl0traversalKey field to the type identified by mdl0rootType field.
The Business Object type. It can have any Business Object type name as a valid value.

TcRuntimeType.description: Geometric Constraint Search Recipe enhances the search results based on constraint data.Mdl0SearchGeomConstraint is a runtime business object created when a search recipe is created having a constraint search term.Mdl0SearchGeomConstraint object is used by 4GD applications and CAD applications which search for constrained and constraining model content.

TcProperty.description: Source Search Criteria on which the constraint search term is to be applied. Output from this search criterion is used to get the additional constraint members in search result based on the process control flag.

This flag indicate how the search result (results from a search execution of mdl0SourceCriteria) is treated to fetch the related constraint data. The flag value is treated bitwise to parse out 4 flags from the single value:First bit - Indicates whether the result should be treated as foreground Second - Indicates whether the result should be treated as backgroundThird - Indicates if foreground members should be appended to the final result output.Fourth - Indicates if background members should be appended to the final result output. E.g.: 6 - 0110 - Treat the search result as background and append foreground members to final search result.

TcRuntimeType.description: Mdl0SearchGroup is a business object which is used to combine multiple search definitions and create a group of them.The search group combines the search definitions using a specific operator which could be AND/OR/NOT.Mdl0SearchGroup is created to process the search operation and destroyed when the search is finished/stopped.The Mdl0SearchGroup may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0SearchGroup is used by 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: A reference to Search Definitions connected by this Search Group. The value of mdl0searchDefs cannot be NULL as a Group cannot exist without atleast two Search definitions.
An integer value that specifies the operator between the various search definitions in the group.Valid values are 0 (AND/Filter), 1 (OR/Include) and 2 (NOT/Exclude)
The name of the group recipe term.

TcRuntimeType.description: Mdl0SearchOptionSet is a business object which is used to store various transfer options provided to a search by the end user.Mdl0SearchOptionSet is created to process the search operation and destroyed when the search is finished/stopped.The Mdl0SearchOptionSet may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0SearchOptionSet is used by 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: A reference to TransferOptionSetImpl object which contains the options selected by user for the search.
Array of strings that specify the option names to be used for the searchIf the value is invalid or NULL the search operation will return an error.
Array of strings that specify the value for the option to match within the searchIf the value is invalid or NULL the search operation will return an error.

TcRuntimeType.description: Mdl0SearchPlaneZone is a business object that represents plane coordinates (originVectorX, originVectorY, originVectorZ, displacement) and operator for spatial search in Teamcenter.Mdl0SearchPlaneZone is created to process the search operation and destroyed when the search is finished/stopped.The Mdl0SearchPlaneZone may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0SearchPlaneZone is used by 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: An integer value that specifies the search operator. Valid values are 0 (above), 1 (below), 2 (intersecting), 3 (above or intersecting) and 4 (below or intersecting).This parameter cannot be NULL.
Array of four double values that defines the criteria plane. The first three double values are normal vector of the plane and the fourth one represents the displacement.This parameter cannot be NULL.

TcRuntimeType.description: Mdl0SearchProximity is a business object that represents source objects or a search for source objects and a proximity distance for spatial search in Teamcenter.Mdl0SearchProximity is created to process the search operation and destroyed when the search is finished/stopped.The Mdl0SearchProximity may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0SearchProximity is used by 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: A double value that specifies a proximity distance (in meters) to be searched from the source objects.The search criteria is always inside or intersects for the proximity search operation. This cannot be changed by the end user.This value cannot be NULL.

Reference to an object of type Mdl0SearchSlctContentImpl which specify the target elements for the search. The target can be specific Design model elements around which the proximity search is performed or another Search Criteria to find out the target Design model elements.This value cannot be NULL.

TcRuntimeType.description: Mdl0SearchResultType is a business object which is used to capture the types of objects that should be returned by the Search. Essentially this is a filter on the search expression to search on specific subclasses of Mdl0ModelElement.Mdl0SearchResultType is created to process the search operation and destroyed when the search is finished/stopped.The Mdl0SearchResultType may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0SearchResultType is used by 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: A list of strings that specify the names of the subtypes of Mdl0ModelElement. The results of the search recipe will be filtered to return only the objects of these types.
Name of the domain view key which stores the domain filter list. NULLS are allowed.

TcRuntimeType.description: Mdl0SearchSavedQuery is a business object that represents saved query name, entry and value pairs of interested criterions for attribute search in Teamcenter.Mdl0SearchSavedQuery is created to process the search operation and destroyed when the search is finished/stopped.The Mdl0SearchSavedQuery may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0SearchSavedQuery is used by 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: Reference to the existing saved query object in Teamcenter to be used for the searchIf the value is invalid or NULL the search operation will return an error.
Array of strings that specify the entry names of the saved query being used for searchIf the value is invalid or NULL the search operation will return an error.
Array of strings that specify the value for the entries to match using the saved query being used for searchIf the value is invalid or NULL the search operation will return an error.

TcRuntimeType.description: The Mdl0SearchSlctContent references to the Model Elements that are result of a specific search. This stores both selected and unselected to differentiate between what the search result is and what the user selected from that resultant set.Mdl0SearchSlctContent could be used in conjunction with a Proximity search to specify the target lines or store explicit include/exclude list provided within a search recipe.Mdl0SearchSlctContent is created to process the search operation and destroyed when the search is finished/stopped.The Mdl0SearchSlctContent may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0SearchSlctContent is used by 4GD applications.

TcProperty.description: Stores the selected model element(s) when used as search criteria storage.Also used to store result model element(s) of the search recipe.
Stores the unselected model element(s) when used as search criteria storage.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0AbsOccFormRelation business object is used to represent a relation where the primary object is a Cpd0DesignElement business object and the secondary is an Absolute Occurrence Form business object.The Absolute Occurrence Form business object is associated with the source BOMLine that is used as input for the Item Realization. The Mdl0AbsOccFormRelation business object is created while performing Item Realization. The Mdl0AbsOccFormRelation business object is a POM_revisable business object.This business object is used by the 4GD application.This business object can be extended by internal downstream applications or external customers. Separate GRM rule may be required if needed.

Mdl0ApplicationModel is an abstract Business Object that represents a container for content forming the elements of a specific application domain model.Mdl0AppicationModel is used to organize and independently manage domain data including positioning model elements and configuring conditional elements.Mdl0ApplicationModel is the parent Business Object based on which product design, partition template or any other domain model business objects will be derived from. Mdl0Application Model is used in 4GD, 4G Partitions, 4G BOM, NGP applications.Downstream Applications and Customers will create sub types of Mdl0ApplciationModel and add custom properties to the sub-type in order to meet their requirements.

TcProperty.description: This property stores a boolean value to indicate whether the Application Model has associated Configurator Context. The values can be true or false.

This is a runtime property that evaluates and stores at runtime a boolean value to indicate whether adding content to the Mdl0ApplicationMode is allowed for the current session. The values can be true or false.

This is a runtime property that evaluates and stores at runtime a boolean value to indicate whether removing content from the Mdl0ApplicationMode is allowed for the current session. The values can be true or false.
IMAN_specification is relation property. IMAN_specification is use to attached different types of dataset, references of business Object
Property mdl0config_product_Name stores name of the Configurator Context associated with the application model.
Namespace of the Effectivity Configurator Product Context associated with the application model.
Namespace of the Variant Configurator Product Context associated with the model.
This property stores name of the Variant Configurator Product Name associated with the model.
IMAN_Rendering is relation property. With IMAN Rendering user can attach geometric image for application model.
This property stores a Boolean value to indicate whether the Application Model has associated Variant Configurator Context. The values can be true or false
This property implements a simple form of BOM compare, for display as an object property.

mdl0RunningProcess is a string property on Application Model which represents the name of the process running on the Application Model. If Snapshot or Restore process is running on Application Model it will return string "Snapshot" or "Restore" respectively else it will return empty string.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0ApprSrchCrtOptionSet is a business object which is used to store various transfer options provided to a search by the end user.Mdl0ApprSrchCrtOptionSet is created when the search recipe having transfer option(s) is saved.The Mdl0ApprSrchCrtOptionSet may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0ApprSrchCrtOptionSet is used by 4GD applications.

Mdl0ApprSrchCrtType is a business object which is used to capture the types of objects that should be returned by the Search. Essentially this is a filter on the search expression to search on specific subclasses of Mdl0ModelElement.Mdl0ApprSrchCrtType is created when the search recipe having search criteria type(s) is saved.The Mdl0ApprSrchCrtType may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0ApprSrchCrtType is used by 4GD applications.

Search Criteria that enhances the search results based on constraint data.Mdl0ApprSrchGeomConstraint object is created when a search recipe is created having a constraint search term. It is a persistent object.Mdl0ApprSrchGeomConstraint object is used by 4GD applications and CAD applications that manage geometric constraints. Mdl0ApprSrchGeomConstraint is inheritable though that is not recommended.
Mdl0ApprSrchIncludeAll object is created when a search recipe is created with include all elements in a model object

The Mdl0ApprSrchSlctContent is used to store references to the Model Elements that are a result of a specific search. This stores both selected and unselected to differentiate between what the search result is and what the user selected from that resultant set.Mdl0ApprSrchSlctContent could be used in conjunction with a Proximity search to specify the target lines or store explicit include/exclude list provided within the search recipe.Mdl0ApprSrchSlctContent is created when the search recipe having selected model element(s) is saved.The Mdl0ApprSrchSlctContent may be extended, but there is no need to do so.Mdl0ApprSrchSlctContent is used by 4GD applications.

The Mdl0AttributeGroup Business Object provides a means to specify additional properties which need to be associated to the Model Element Business Object with the Mdl0AttachAttrGroup relation.This Mdl0AttributeGroup Business Object would typically have custom properties grouped together into one object based on their type. Typically the properties of one type will be added to one specific sub-type of Mdl0AttributeGroup. This enables the user to apply independently access and load the properties that are grouped together into the Mdl0AtrtibuteGroup Business Object, which cannot be done if the properties were defined on the primary Model Element Business Object. The Mdl0AttributeGroup Object will be used by 4GD and its downstream applications.Downstream Applications as well as Customers should sub-type this Mdl0AttributeGroup Business Object and define the properties they need.

An Mdl0Baseline object represents a baseline of a 4GD model. A Mdl0Baseline can be revised, following the Item model.Unlike Item/BVR in general, Baselines do not form structures and are intended to be used by 4G applications only to represent stable snapshot of the data

Mdl0BaselineDefinition defines baseline content. It references the source model to search, and holds both the search recipe and configuration information to apply.Baseline Definition is managed automatically by the system as part of Mdl0BaselineRevision.

TcProperty.description: The model object, configured using the definition cparam.This property is computed by the system and can be used to access correctly configured contents of the baseline.

TcStandardType.description: An Mdl0Baseline object represents a baseline of a 4GD model. A Mdl0Baseline can be revised, following the Item model.

An Mdl0BaselineReference relation is used to attach additional, reference data to an Mdl0BaselineRevision. For example ChangeItemRevision Business Objects could be attached to Mdl0BaselineRevision using MDL-attach-changes-to-baselines workflow handler to indicate changes included in the baseline.This business object is used by 4GD and any downstream applications that consume the Application Model Elements component.
An Mdl0Baseline object represents a baseline of a 4GD model. A Mdl0Baseline can be revised, following the Item model.

Represents a revision of Mdl0Baseline, containing revision-specific properties. Mdl0BaselineRevision represents an immutable Snapshot or Baseline of content in an Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel). A Snapshot can be used to capture working data in an Application Model, and it is possible for the content stored in Snapshots to be restored back to working state, as compare to Baselines which only capture Released state of an Application Model and cannot be restored. Such Application Models that support Snapshot cannot make use of Change Spaces.

TcProperty.description: Historical configuration date (NULLDATE if not set).

An Mdl0SupportingBaseline relation is used to attach a secondary supporting Mdl0BaselineRevision to a primary aggregate Mdl0BaselineRevision.One or more supporting baselines contribute their content to the aggregate baseline. This facilitates easier management of baselined content of large models.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0ConditionalArtifact is an abstract sub business object of Mdl0ModelArtifact. It adds effectivity and variant expressions to specify conditions when this object is applicable in the Application Model. It serves as the abstract base object for the different types of Mdl0ConditionalArtifact in 4GD (4th Generation Design).

TcProperty.description: Runtime property representing the effectivity formula which is used to configure this object. Its value is identical to that of runtime property mdl0allowed_eff_formula if no roll down effect is applied. When there is a roll down, its value is filtered by the roll down and limited by mdl0allowed_eff_formula. Its value may be a subset of the effectivity range returned by property mdl0allowed_eff_formula.
Deprecated: A user friendly text representation of the effectivity expression.

Runtime property representing effectivity formula as it was assigned directly to this object. It specifies the maximum effectivity range for which this object is applicable. This property supports a system as well as a display format. The value might be super set of the effectivity range returned by property mdl0effectivity_formula.
Deprecated: A user friendly text representation of the "applicability" effectivity expression.

Runtime property representing variant formula as it was assigned directly to this object. It specifies the variant conditions for which this object is applicable. This property supports a system as well as a display format. The value might be super set of the variant conditions returned by property mdl0variant_formula.

Runtime property representing the variant formula which is used to configure this object when variant rule is applied. Its value is identical to that of runtime property mdl0allowed_var_formula if no roll down effect is applied. When there is a roll down, its value is filtered by the roll down and limited by mdl0allowed_var_formula. Its value may be a subset of the variant conditions returned by property mdl0allowed_var_formula.
Runtime property indicating if the revision is configured by applying revision rules. It is set to true if the object is configure by revision rules and set to false otherwise.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0ConditionalElement is an abstract sub business object of Mdl0ModelElement . It also adds effectivity and variant expressions to specify conditions when this object is applicable in an Mdl0ApplicationModel. It serves as the abstract base object for the different types of Mdl0ModelElement in 4GD (4th Generation Design).

TcProperty.description: A list of major revision siblings including itself.

Runtime property representing the effectivity formula which is used to configure this object. Its value is identical to that of runtime property mdl0allowed_eff_formula if no roll down effect is applied. When there is a roll down, its value is filtered by the roll down and limited by mdl0allowed_eff_formula. Its value may be a subset of the effectivity range returned by property mdl0allowed_eff_formula.
Deprecated: A user friendly text representation of effectivity expression.
A system friendly (parsable) text representation (in configurator language) of the "applicability" effectivity expression.
Deprecated: A user friendly text representation of the "applicability" effectivity expression.
Runtime property indicating if the object is revisable by currently logged user. It is set to true if the user can revise the object and set to false otherwise.

Runtime property representing variant formula as it was assigned directly to this object. It specifies the variant conditions for which this object is applicable. This property supports a system as well as a display format. The value might be super set of the variant conditions returned by property mdl0variant_formula.

Runtime property representing the variant formula which is used to configure this object when variant rule is applied. Its value is identical to that of runtime property mdl0allowed_var_formula if no roll down effect is applied. When there is a roll down, its value is filtered by the roll down and limited by mdl0allowed_var_formula. Its value may be a subset of the variant conditions returned by property mdl0allowed_var_formula.
Runtime property indicating if the revision is configured by applying revision rules. It is set to true if the object is configured by revision rules and set to false otherwise.

TcStandardType.description: A concrete subclass of Positioned Geometry representing (default) positioned design content within an Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel).The Mdl0DefaultGeometry business object is used internally by the 4GD application. There is no UI exposure for this business object.

This object binds together all major revisions (Mdl0ConditionalElement) of the same object.Threads are managed automatically by the system as part of Mdl0ConditionalElement Create/Revise/SaveAs operations.

TcProperty.description: This property points to a major revision (Mdl0ConditionalElement) which satisfies the configuration criteria, i.e. revision rule, effectivity, etc.This property is computed and relies on the configuration criteria to be available through the cparam of the Mdl0ElementThread

TcStandardType.description: A Saved State holds an iteration of the set of members of a Geometric Constraint Bucket.A new Saved State will be automatically created when an application attempts to add or replace a foreground member into an existing Saved State which has all its foreground members already having a released status. This permits the now older Saved State to be cleanly loaded when only those released members are being loaded into the CAD application.A Saved State may also be referenced by an Mdl0PositionedModelElement (or rather the associated Mdl0PositionedGeometry object's mdl0DefiningConstraintState attribute) in order to show which constraint state last impacted the position or shape of the Positioned Model Element.

Mdl0GeomCnstrntCollection represents a geometric constraint group and its (foreground/background) Constraint Members, which may be considered either foreground or background members.Storage of the group details and its members is on an associated Mdl0GeomConstraintBucket (references the collection by mdl0OwningObject) and behavior is via the Mdl0GeomConstraintContainer behavior class.Used by NX to manage constraint groups where various background and foreground positioned elements have constraints among them that control or constraint the position of some of the foreground elements.

TcProperty.description: Runtime list of foreground members of the Geometric Constraint Collection as precisely referenced in the latest iteration of the geometric constraint container. Deleted or remote members are dropped from this list.May be NULL if no foreground members exist.

Runtime list of background members of the Geometric Constraint Collection as precisely referenced in the latest iteration of the geometric constraint container. Deleted or remote members are dropped from this list.May be NULL if no background members exist.

Total number of Foreground members of Geometric Constraint Collection as precisely referenced in the latest iteration of the geometric constraint container. Deleted or remote members are counted for this value.

Total number of Background members of Geometric Constraint Collection as precisely referenced in the latest iteration of the geometric constraint container. Deleted or remote members are counted for this value.

Total number of Stubbed Foreground members of Geometric Constraint Collection. This number indicates how many foreground members have not yet been replicated to the current site and are hence not present in the mdl0ForegroundMembers list.

Total number of Stubbed Background members of Geometric Constraint Collection. This number indicates how many background members have not yet been replicated to the current site and are hence not present in the mdl0BackgroundMembers list.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0GeomConnGroup Business Object models a connection between a given pair of end equipment in a routing.A routing design starts with 2D piping and instrumentation diagram that logically represents how a given pair of equipment, referred as end equipment, are connected. For example, these end equipment could be a pump and a tank. The design then proceeds to 3D modeling of the piping and instrumentation. This activity results in creation of Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects realizing the 2D logical design. For instance, pipe stocks are modeled.The connection, which is basically a collection of all the Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects connecting the end equipment and the end equipment themselves, is modeled by Mdl0GeomConnGroup. Mdl0GeomConnGroup has a logical identity property (mdl0LogicalId) referring to the 2D logical diagram. Mdl0GeomConnGroup is used by CAD applications providing Piping and Instrumentation (P&ID) feature.

TcProperty.description: mdl0GroupLinks refer to Mdl0GeomGroupLink objects in a connection (Mdl0GeomConnGroup).Each Mdl0GeomGroupLink object captures one or two Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects that are participating in a routing.The Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects participating in a routing have corresponding Mdl0GeomLink objects. The mdl0LinkId value on a Mdl0GeomGroupLink object and mdl0LinkId value on Mdl0GeomLink object corresponding to the positioned Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects it captures will be same.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0GeomConstraintBucket represents a bucket of constraint data managed on behalf of an owning object having Mdl0ConstraintContainer behavior (such as a Geometric Constraint Collection object - Mdl0GeomCnstrntCollection)Mdl0GeomConstraintBucket is the primary storage object for the Mdl0GeomConstraintContainer behavior. Other storage classes are the Mdl0GeomCnstrntBuckSavState and Mdl0GeomConstraintMember.The bucket tracks members over time by holding multiple iterations (also call saved states) which are created only under specific conditions (see the Mdl0GeomCnstrntBuckSavState's description for details.)Mdl0GeomConstraintContainer behavior provides methods to determine the best iteration to retrieve when given a configuration context, as well as methods to retrieve an iteration's content either precise or configured (when configured, a member may be dropped out or configured to a different revision than the member precisely specifies based on the input configuration context.)Mdl0GeomConstraintBucket is indirectly used by CAD applications that leverage the Mdl0GeomCnstrntCollection to track constraint data.

Mdl0GeomConstraintMember represents the association of a positionable model element (Mdl0PositionedModelElement) as a foreground or background member of a Geometric Constraint Collection for some specific iteration or range of iterations (see Mdl0GeomCnstrntBuckSavState).It is a low-level storage class for any geometric constraint container (e.g. objects having Mdl0GeomConstraintContainer behavior). The entire set or a subset of these member records are used in determining what the members of a given iteration are and also which iteration to load for a given set of potential members (not all may still be present in the best chosen iteration.)CAD tools may leverage geometric constraint containers to manage constrained 4GD elements in application models (Mdl0ApplicationModel).

Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects are associated with Mdl0GeomConnGroup through Mdl0GeomGroupLink objects and Mdl0GeomLink objects.Each Mdl0GeomGroupLink object captures Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects that are participating in a routing.Mdl0GeomGroupLink has an inherited attribute, mdl0TargetObject, which is a reference to routing connection (Mdl0GeomConnGroup).The Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects participating in a routing connection have corresponding Mdl0GeomLink objects. The mdl0LinkId attribute value on Mdl0GeomLink object is same as mdl0LinkId value on Mdl0GeomGroupLink that is adding the positioned model element(s) to routing connection (Mdl0GeomConnGroup).

Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects are associated with Mdl0GeomConnGroup through Mdl0GeomGroupLink objects and Mdl0GeomLink objects.Mdl0GeomLink object has a reference to its target object via an attribute, mdl0TargetObject. The target object is an MdlPositionedGeometry; the positioned object (mdl0positioned_object) of which is a participant of Mdl0GeomConnGroup. Mdl0GeomLink object has another attribute, mdl0LinkId. The value of this attribute is same as the mdl0LinkId attribute value on Mdl0GeomGroupLink object; thus associating the Mdl0PositionedModelElement object to its Mdl0GeomConnGroup.

TcProperty.description: This runtime value is used to infer whether the CAD application has to repeat the geometric validation or not.If the target Mdl0PositionedModelElement has not undergone any change in shape (mdl0shape_lmd on Mdl0PositionedGeometry) or position (mdl0position_lmd on Mdl0PositionedGeometry), after the geometry was last validated (mdl0GeometryLMD on this Mdl0GeomLink), then this value is returned as true indicating that the link is still valid. Else, a false is returned indicating that the link needs to be validated again.

This runtime value returns lists the Mdl0GeomConnGroups in which the target Mdl0PositionedModelElement is a participant.Note that even though it is being mentioned as "target Mdl0PositionedModelElement", in terms of the datamodel, the target of Mdl0GeomLink is Mdl0PositionedGeometry. It is Mdl0PositionedGeometry that captures what the Mdl0PosistionedModelElement is (through mdl0positioned_object).

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0LinkReference is an abstract base Business Object for Business Objects that link a given pair of Mdl0PositionedModelElement objects or just associate an Mdl0PositionedModelElement to a Mdl0GeomConnGroup.The Business Objects extended from Mdl0LinkReference, namely Mdl0GeomLink and Mdl0GeomGroupLink are used by a routing application when capturing the routing information.The target object (mdl0TargetObject) is the object being associated / paired in an Mdl0GeomConnGroup. Note that even though it is being mentioned as "target Mdl0PositionedModelElement", in terms of the datamodel, the target of Mdl0LinkReference is a Mdl0PositionedGeometry. Attribute mdl0positioned_object on Mdl0PositionedGeometry captures what the Mdl0PosistionedModelElement is.The mdl0LinkId helps in this association/pairing. Please look into Mdl0GeomLink and Mdl0GeomGroupLink description for further details.

The Mdl0ManagedAttrGroup Business Object provides a means to specify extended set of properties for Model Elements, when the lifecycle or security access of the attribute group is different than the model element itself. The Mdl0ManagedAttrGroup business object will be attached to Model Elements with the Mdl0AttachAttrGroup relation where the Model Element is the primary of the relation and the Mdl0ManagedAttributeGroup is the secondary of the relation.This enables the user to manage independent access and separate lifecycle for these objects.The Mdl0AttributeGroup Object will be used by 4th Generation Design and its downstream applications.Downstream Applications as well as Customers should sub-type this Mdl0AttributeGroup Business Object and define custom properties.

Mdl0ModelArtifact is an abstract class used to manifest model contents which are not Workspace objects.Mdl0ModelArtifact object can only be created in an Application Model. It serves as the abstract base object for different types of Mdl0ModelArtifact in 4GD(4th Generation Design).

TcProperty.description: Runtime property indicating if an ongoing SaveAs operation is to be performed for inter-model copy. It is set to true by Teamcenter while SaveAs for inter-model copy is being performed and set to false otherwise.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0ModelElement is an abstract business object used to manifest model content with workspace object behaviors.Mdl0ModelElement object can only be created in an Mdl0ApplicationModel. Teamcenter does not require the user to have write access to the Application Model to create Mdl0ModelElement object in it and remove Mdl0ModelElement object from it. Attribute Group object can be attached to manage a group of related attributes where different access rules are required. Manage Attribute Group can be attached to manage a group of related attributes in a separate lifecycle from the Model Element.It serves as the abstract base object for the different types of Mdl0ModelElement in 4GD (4th Generation Design).

TcProperty.description: IMAN_specification relation that attaches other objects. It is used to attach objects like Folder, Envelope.
Mdl0AttachAttrGroup relation that attaches Managed Attribute Groups. It is used to attach Attribute Group and Managed Attribute Group.

Runtime property holding the list of the Attribute Groups and Managed Attribute Groups which are created for this Model Element object but are not saved in Teamcenter yet. They will be saved when the Model Element object is saved.
Deprecated: This property implements a simple form of BOM compare, for display as an object property.
Runtime property returning a list of Attribute Groups and Managed Attribute Groups which are attached to this Model Element through relation Mdl0AttachAttGroup.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0ModelProcessState represents the information of the process ( Snapshot or Restore ) running on the Application Model supporting Snapshot. It is marked lightweight object as its internal object and it has short life span and it will not participate in multisite and search usecases.

A concrete subclass of Positioned Geometry representing positioned design content before position/shape override within an Application Model (e.g. a Product Design). This business object is created only when there is a shape or position override on the Positioned Model Element. It will be deleted after both the shape and position overrides are deleted.

Mdl0OverrideRelation represents the association between a Mdl0DefaultGeometry and a CAD specific Dataset for geometry override. The primary object is Mdl0DefaultGeometry and secondary object is a CAD specific Dataset. For shape override created by NX, the secondary is NXApplicationDatasetMdl0OverrideRelation is created when shape override is created on Mdl0PositionedModelElement in 4GD(4th Generation Design) and destroyed when the shape override is removed. It is inheritable.

Mdl0PositionedGeometry is an abstract storage class for the Mdl0Positionable behavior that contains both position and geometric information of a positioned object. Position information is used to position the object referenced by mdl0positioned_object. It is used by 4th generation design foundation and CAD tools that leverage positioned model content in application models.

TcStandardType.description: Mdl0PositionedModelElement is an abstract sub business object of Mdl0ConditionalElement. It represents the independently managed, positioned design content within an Application Model. It has Mdl0Positionable behavior which manages its geometric and position information.In 4th generation design, sub business objects of Mdl0PositionedModelElement like Cpd0DesignElements and Cpd0DesignFeatures are used to model the design content of aCpd0CollaborativeDesign.

TcProperty.description: Reference to related positioned geometry object. NULL value is not permitted as it always has a positioned geometry object.
If the element has been positioned by a geometric constraint, this property will return the constraint container by which the element was position constrained.
One or more Constraint Collections in which the design component is a precise background member. This could be null if the design component is not a background member of any Constraint Collection.

Reference Geometry relation.It is used to reflect a geometric dependency of one design component on another. NX and other CAD tools allow associatively copying of geometry from one design component (the source) to another design component (the target). As the source design component changes, the target design component can be updated to reflect the modifications in the source.
Property to return overriding dataset which gets created while applying shape or position override on positioned model element.

TcStandardType.description: This represents an expression dependency of one Mdl0ModelElement object on another. The target Mdl0ModelElement is the primary object attached to the Mdl0ReferenceExpression; while the secondary object is the source Mdl0ModelElement object that the expression is being referenced from. As an expression in the source Mdl0ModelElement changes, the target Mdl0ModelElement can be updated to reflect the modifications of the expression in the source object.

This models the relation that relates Cpd0DesignElement and Cpd0DesignControlElement objects to other Cpd0DesignElement objects used in their geometric construction/definition.These relations are generated in CAD systems, and indicate associative geometric relationship between the related objects. These may include points, axes or planes defined as reference geometry in the CAD system.The primary object for a Mdl0ReferenceGeometry object is the object into which geometry was referenced or copied, and the secondary is the object from which it was referenced or copied.An example illustrating this is copying the centerline of a tank outlet and the centerline of a corresponding pump inlet when constructing a mechanical routing, in which case the Cpd0DesignControlElement object would have two reference geometry relations, pointing to the tank and pump Cpd0DesignElement objects respectively.

Mdl0SubsetDefaults is a type of Attribute Group (Mdl0AttributeGroup) used to store target properties for model content added into a subset.Mdl0SubsetDefaults may be related (via Mdl0AttachAttrGroup) to a single Mdl0SubsetDefinition. However, this default relation is not supported by any behavior currently. Any consuming application must provide their own behavior to apply the default values to the related subset content at the desired time.Mdl0SubsetDefaults is an abstract class and hence other templates and applications are expected to sub-type it for their own needs. Currently this is done in the Partition and 4GD (4th Generation Design) templates.

Mdl0SubsetDefinition represents a subset of an Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel) based on a stored Recipe (ApprSearchCriteria) that is executed to view the subset content.The subset content is the model content objects that match the recipe's search criteria and unlike its parent (Fnd0RecipeContainer), all the search criteria is applied only to the referenced model (via mdl0model_object ).Mdl0SubsetDefinition is used extensively in 4GD applications and most applications built on the 4GD foundation.

TcProperty.description: Runtime property listing the attached Attribute Groups (Mdl0AttrGroup) and Managed Attribute Groups (Mdl0ManagedAttrGroup) associated to this subset definition via the mdl0AttachAttrGroup relation.An empty list may be returned if there are no such attached objects.

Between the time of creation and the initial save of the Mdl0SubsetDefinition, this runtime property will contain a list of attribute groups (Mdl0AttributeGroup) and Managed attribute groups (Mdl0ManagedAttrGroup) of various types that have been created but not yet saved. The newly created types are specified on the createInput for the Mdl0SubsetDefinition in the mdl0pending_AttachAttrGroup and mdl0pending_AttcAttrRlType properties.After the initial save, this list will be empty.

A runtime configured reference to the application model, configured according to minor revisions or change context. This reference can be used to query for model content configured according to the same change context or minor revision.mdl0ConfiguredModel is only meant to be read, as it does not store a value, but rather compute one.The configured model will never be NULL, but may be the same as the mdl0model_object if no configuration is associated either persistently or dynamically to the Mdl0SubsetDefinition.

Compound property which exposes mdl0bounding_box property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It represents the bounding box array in the following order {min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x, max_y, max_z)

Compound property which exposes mdl0DefiningIteration property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It references a Geometric Constraint Bucket Save State object of a Geometric Constraint Collection to restrict only one foreground membership for a Design Component revision. It may be NULL which indicates the positioned object is not constrained directly, but may still be configured into a constraint container if a different revision is a member.
Compound property which exposes mdl0direct_model_data property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It references to the Direct Model Dataset. It may be NULL.

Compound property which exposes mdl0ExcludeFromSpatialSrch property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It indicates if spatial search will exclude it from search result. For example, a cutting tool that is not part of a design and used to create Geometric cuts would set this value to true.

Compound property which exposes mdl0GeomLinks property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It is the list of geometric links that specify the connections between this object and other Positioned Model Element object in a mechanical routing.

Compound property which exposes mdl0IsAbsolutelyPositioned property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. Indicate if Mdl0PositionedGeomtry is positioned explicitly in a constraint.

Compound property which exposes mdl0IsUsedInConstraint property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It indicates if the Mdl0PositionedGeometry has ever been used in a constraint either as a foreground or a background in a constraint.
Compound property which exposes mdl0jt_file property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It represents the JT File. It may be NULL.

Compound property which exposes mdl0position_lmd property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It represents the last-modified-date (LMD) of the CAD position data (transform). This attribute factors into the evaluation of mdl0sync_secondary_revision property on Mdl0CopyStableRelations

Compound property which exposes mdl0relative_to property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It references the object which the position is relative to. NULL value is allowed and indicates it is not positioned relative to any other object.

Compound property which exposes mld0shape_lmd property from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. Represents the last-modified-date (LMD) of the CAD shape data used to create the positioned object. This attribute factors into the evaluation of mdl0sync_secondary_revision property on Mdl0CopyStableRelations.
Compound property exposing mdl0ThumnailDataset from the Default Geometry object referenced by mdl0positioned_geometry. It references the thumbnail Dataset for shape override. It may be NULL.

ServiceInterface.description:
This service provides operations that enable searching conditional model elements (Mdl0ConditionalElement) in a given application model. An application model could be a product design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign in the case of CPD).
Search service provides the ability to search for conditional model elements using various search recipes (spatial and nonspatial). Search service also provides the ability to save a search recipe in the database and retrieve a previously stored recipe.

Use Cases:
Search service is used by the CPD application to implement Searching CPD Design Components (Cpd0DesignElement) within a product design. Search is a generic search capability that could be used to search conditional model elements within a given application model(Mdl0ApplicationModel). Please refer to the CPD Server Functional Specifications for detailed descriptions on application model and model element data schema.
AppModel search supports searching of model elements based on different search expressions. The search expressions could be

Spatial:
    Box Zone Expression (Mdl0SearchBoxZone) defines a rectangular (axis aligned) box, defined in a 3d space, which could be used to find Conditional Model Elements that are either inside/outside/intersecting the 3 dimensional box.
    Plane Zone Expression (Mdl0SearchPlaneZone) defines a 3d plane and the search expression could define to look for Conditional Model Elements above/below/intersecting the plane.
    Proximity Expression (Mdl0SearchProximity) used to find Conditional Model Elements that are spatially nearby a given set of other Conditional Model Elements.

Non Spatial:
    Saved Query Expression (Mdl0SearchSavedQuery) used to search Conditional Model Elements with specific property values. Accepts wildcards for property values.
    Include Expression (Mdl0SearchSlctContent) specific set of Model Elements that are included as part of the search result.
    Exclude Expression (Mdl0SearchGroup) specific set of Model Elements that are excluded from the search result.
    Partition Expression (Ptn0SearchPartition) Model Elements that are members of a particular set of Partitions in the given Product Design.
    Closure Query Expression (Mdl0SearchOptionSet) Return related objects, selected by the given option set and closure rule, as part of the search results.

The above search expressions could be joined using AND/OR operators to form complex Search Recipes. Also the results of the execution of a Search Recipe could be constrained to return only a given set of object types. For e.g. the results of a Search Recipe could be restricted to return only Cpd0DesignElement objects. The callers could also use NOT operator to negate any of the non spatial expressions above and combine them in a Search Recipe (Note that NOT is a Unary operator and it accepts only one expression to negate unlike AND/OR which combines multiple expressions).

Search Service is typically used to perform the following operations:

Create Configuration Context for a CPD session: A CPD client session could call createOrUpdateConfigurations to create one or more ConfigurationContext objects that hold the RevisionRule and Effectivity Rule and Variant Rule that is required to configure the results of a Search execution. These ConfigurationContext objects are runtime objects that could be used repeatedly by the client throughout the session (over different search operations).

Create Search Expressions to perform a Search (or Save a Search Recipe): Before executing a search or saving a recipe, this is a prerequired step to create the elemental search expressions (both Spatial and non Spatial).

Execute a Search Recipe: Executes a complex search recipe formed using the various search expression combinations and constrained using the search scope (Application Model, Search Types). The results of a executing a search could be sorted using the one or more of the attributes properties of the returned object type. Also the number of objects that should be returned to the caller can be controlled by setting the defaultLoadCount. If the default load count is set to zero then all the results are returned in one shot.
If the default load count is set to a non zero value, then the caller will be returned a search cursor which could be used to get search results as and when it is required. Also an active search cursor could be released by calling the stopSearch operation.
Save/Retrieve a stored Search Recipe: Save and Retrieve a complex search recipe in the Teamcenter database. Recipes are not independent objects and they would have to be stored in an object that exhibits a RecipeContainer behavior. In CPD, There are four objects that exhibit RecipeContainer behavior as of now. They are Mdl0SubsetDefinition object to store a search recipe, Ptn0Partition a dynamic partition that finds members based on a search operation and Cpd0DesignSubsetInstance object that selects a subset of a Product Design using a search recipe and instantiates into a Workset, and Mdl0BaselineDefinition an object which stores a recipe for use with an Mdl0BaselineRevision.

Sample code:
Typically following is the sequence of operations to perform a Search:
1. Call createOrUpdateConfigurations and create a ConfigurationContext with a valid RevisionRule (optionally with effectivity and variant configuration).
2.Call createSearchExpressions and create the elemental search expressions.
3.Create the Search Expression Sets to join the elemental search expressions to a complex search recipe.
4.Call executeSearch with the complex Search Expression Set. executeSearch will return a default set of conditional elements (defined by the defaultLoadCount).
5.Call fetchNextSearchResults repeatedly to get further results based on the search and each time this operation could be called with its own defaultLoadCount value.
6.    Optionally stopSearch could be called to clean up the results and this call would indicate that the caller is no longer interested in getting back the remaining search results.
Apart from execution of a search query, there are two operations that help the callers to save a Search Recipe and enquire the contents of a persisted Search Recipe. The setRecipes2 call saves a Search Recipe and it requires a Search Container object to persist the recipe. Currently in CPD application, this could be one of either Cpd0DesignSubsetInstance or Ptn0Partition or Mdl0SubsetDefinition or Mdl0BaselineDefinition. The getRecipes2 call returns the search expressions and their combinations (as Search Expression Sets) of a stored recipe.
The sample in soa_client.zip, com.teamcenter.cpdsearch.SearchServiceSOASampleTest.java shows the use of Search operations for the following 2 use cases:
1.Execute a Search with a complex recipe (Saved Query combined with Box Zone and the results restricted to Cpd0DesignElement objects)
2.Save and Retrieve a complex recipe on a Recipe Container object

Struct.description:
ConfigExpression is a recursive data structure which can represent an expression tree by referencing subexpressions of the same data type. The leaf nodes of this tree are ConfigExpression that compare to a value, such as Unit 42, or a Date. The value is given as a ConfigOption, e.g. the option value “42” for the option family “Unit” in family namespace “Teamcenter::”. The opcode parameter of the ConfigExpression structure defines how this ConfigExpression compares to that value, e.g. operator code “5” for “Unit 42” defines the expression “[Teamcenter::]Unit = 42” because “5” is the “EQUAL” operator. The operator code “14” for “Unit 42” defines the expression “[Teamcenter::]Unit < 42” because “14” is the “LESS THAN” operator.

The ConfigExpression structure is interpreted as NULL if it has the following values:
    • subExpressions: An empty vector.
    • value: A NULL ConfigOption structure.
    • opCode: -1
    • formula: A NULL ConfigFormula structure.
    • effectivityTable: An empty vector.
Struct.name: ConfigExpression

StructElement.description:
A list of sub expressions to be combined with opcode.subExpressions and value must not both be present. If neither subExpressions nor value are present, the expression is treated as the identity element (A mathematical term) for all opCode values. An identity element is a special type of element of a set with repsect to a binary operation on that set, which leaves other elements unchanged when combined with them.

For exmple if (S,*) be a set S with a binary operation AND on it. Then an element e of S is called a left identity if e AND a = a for all a in S, and a right identity if a AND e = a for all a in S. If e is both a left identity and a right identity, then it is called a two-sided identity, or simply an identity element.

If neither <font face="courier" height="10">subExpressions</font> nor <font face="courier" height="10">optionValue</font> are present, the expression is treated as the identity element for all <font face="courier" height="10">opCode</font> values.

This operation creates a configuration context (ConfigurationContext) object (or updates a configuration context object). In CPD, the configuration information is kept track using a Configuration Context object. This object is not persisted in the Database. It is just created and kept alive until the session is active and destroyed when the user logs out.
A configuration context keeps track of the Revision Rule (with any attached Effectivity Conditions) (and in the future would keep track of variant rule as well) created/used by a client session. In Teamcenter 9.1.0, minor revisioning is not supported in CPD. When minor revisioning is introduced in Teamcenter 10.1.0, then the configuration context will also serve the purpose of allocating a cparam for the corresponding Revision Rule used by the client session.
cparam is an object used by the POM revisioning framework to configure the correct minor revision of a reviseable object being used.
A configuration context created could be used by the caller during executeSearch or any other operation that requires the revision and effectivity configuration settings.

Configuration conditions are specified by a ConfigurationContext object, which provides revision and unit effectivity rule information. OperationTemplate.description:
The operation clones (Deep copy) model elements from an application model ( referred as source model ) into another application model or within the same application model ( referred as target model ). Elements come from source application model, either manually or via search criteria to be copied into a second application model. The same source content may be cloned multiple times into the same or different target model. No associations are maintained between related objects in the source and target models, therefore there is no capacity to update any cloned content in the target model.

The newly created objects in the target model are fully populated meaning they are persistently created in the context of the target model. The object type and category of the newly created objects will remain same in the target model. For example, a Design Component (Cpd0DesignElement) of category Shape from a source model is cloned into a target model, the category and the object type of the newly created object in the target model will still be the same as the object in the source model. Model elements when cloned across two different source models will be re-identified in the target model. For example, upon cloning new IDs will be assigned to the Design Component objects in the target model.

The elements to be included from the source to the target model can be either an explicit list of elements or results from a recipe. List of elements from the source model to be explicitly included (via multi-select action) can be passed to this operation for cloning the content into the target model.

Note: Internally BMIDE deep copy rules will be used to traverse and clone the source objects.


Preconditions:
1)    The source application model is with some pre-existing model content.
2)    Target application model already exists.
3)    Partitions (Member owns the membership) are pre created in target model if memberships are expected to be copied over to target model.


Cloning in the context of Partitions:

Note: Partitions are not cloned as part of this operation.

Application must leverage on Partition clone functionality to clone partition from one application model into another application model but the model content that resides in the source application model are cloned into the new application model using cloneModelContent Operation.

In order to create Partition breakdowns also in the target model, the applications must follow a two-step process.
1)    Perform Partition Template Clone using existing clonePartitions service operation to copy partitions from one model to another.
2)    Perform Template Clone with model content using the cloneModelContent service operation.

If the initial elements would reference partitions (member owned partitions) in the source application model, membership objects will be also be cloned if the target models have the same partitions else the model elements will be cloned as unassigned members. If same Partition memberships exist both in source model and target model then they are not recreated instead the existing memberships are retained.

Note:
1)    If the source model contains a reuse design component, then all its subordinate design components will be cloned. The system will warn and stop if the user is trying to clone only subordinate design component without its reuse design component.
2)    Delete on cloned content in the target model deletes the selected object alone. If the selected object to delete is a reuse Design Component, then all its subordinates will also be deleted.
3)    If the category of the newly created target object has to be different from source object types then it is Application's/Customer's responsibility to manage any such mappings through extension points provided by the infrastructure.


Note:

1) If the source model contain a reuse design component, then all its subordinate design components will be cloned. This is control by a business object contants called "cloneReuseAlongWithSubordinates". If the value of this constant is true, then reuse and its full chain of subordinates will be cloned togther, else reuse or the selected subordinate will be ignore.

2) Delete on cloned content in the target model deletes the selected object alone. If the selected object to delete is a reuse Design Component , then all its subordinates will also be deleted.

3) Variants and Effectivity conditions will not be carry forwarded onto the target objects in the target model by default alternatively this behavior can be controlled by a business object constant "cloneObjectsWithVariantExpr" , "cloneObjectsWithEffectivityExpr" . If the value of the contant is "true" then Variants or effectivity expressions will copied from source object.

Refer to TDOC for more information on prerequisites on Variant and effectivity expression carry over from source application model to target application model.

Return the aggregate recipe for each given recipe container. Recipe containers are not modified by this operation; however the aggregate recipes returned are suitable for storage using the operation setRecipes2.
    
For an Mdl0BaselineDefinition recipe container, the aggregate recipe is formed from the baseline definition recipe and the recipe of each supporting baseline (see relation Mdl0SupportingBaseline) in the following way:

1. The aggregate recipe is set to a copy of the baseline definition recipe.

2. Each supporting recipe is assigned a name using the display name of its owning Mdl0Baseline.

3. For each supporting recipe group:
If the aggregate group contains one or more recipe groups which match the assigned name: the contents of each group is replaced with a copy of the supporting recipe.
Else: the aggregate group is appended to the recipe, using a recipe group with the assigned name.

4. New groups are appended using the OR operator.

For all other recipe containers the aggregate recipe is identical to the recipe returned by operation getRecipes2.

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation retrieves the stored recipe against a set of recipe container objects. The persistent objects used to store the search recipe in Teamcenter are objects that do not have lifecycle by itself, so they are always associated to objects that exhibit the RecipeContainer behavior. This operation additionally supports retrieving of the domain view key name stored in the search criteria. It will return the saved key name and the resulting searchType list that was populated from that key’s associated list of types to filter. For adhoc search only filter list filter list will be returned.
In the current CPD application there are four objects that exhibit RecipeContainer behavior. They are:

Mdl0SubsetDefinition: object to store a search recipe (without the results).
Ptn0Partition: A dynamic partition that executes the search recipe to find its members.
Cpd0DesignSubsetInstance: A realization object that takes a subset of a Product Design and instantiates into a Workset.
Mdl0BaselineDefinition: object to store a search recipe (without the results) for use an Mdl0BaselineRevision.

The retrieved recipe from the recipe container is translated to the data structures defined in the search operation and then it is presented back to the caller.

This operation additionally supports retrieving of the domainViewKeyName stored in the search criteria. Domain view key is the name of the preference which holds the search filter type list. If the domainViewKeyName is available then this operation will return the domainViewKeyName and the search filter type list that was stored from the preference value at the time of creation. For adhoc searches (where only filter list was passed while creating recipe) only search filter type list will be returned. If both domainViewKeyName and an explicit searchType list were provided as input while creating the recipe than the filter list returned by this operation is the one that was explicitly passed to the set operation and not the one retrieved from the preference. The later scenario should be only used for client-driven cloning of a recipes as a later update of the recipe in a normal client flow should send only the domainViewKeyName in order to retrieve any potential update from preferences.

The persistent objects used to store the search recipe in Teamcenter are objects that do not have lifecycle by itself, so they are always associated to objects that exhibit the RecipeContainer behavior. In the current CPD application there are four objects that exhibit RecipeContainer behavior. They are:

Mdl0SubsetDefinition: object to store a search recipe (without the results).

When providing a search scope, either an ad-hoc search type filter (searchType list) or a domain view key (domainViewKeyName) may be given. A domain view key is the preference name which stores an associated list of search filter types. The preference pointed to by the domainViewKeyName will be read to fetch the search filter types, which will be stored with the recipe and will be used in search to filter the results. In most cases other than no filtering scope, only one of searchType or domainViewKeyName should be provided as input.

If both domainViewKeyName and explicit searchType list are provided as input then they will both be set without any derivation of the searchType list values from preferences, in order to support any rare client-driven cloning of a recipe use case. Note that any later update of the recipe in a normal client flow should send only the domainViewKeyName in order to retrieve any potential update from preferences.

Note that the recipe is deleted when its container object is deleted.

Thus, in this case value "bom_properties_based_de_search" is populated for compositeSearchType field.

Operation.description:
The operation clones (Deep copy) model elements from an application model ( referred as source model ) into another application model or within the same application model ( referred as target model ). Elements come from source application model, either manually or via search criteria to be copied into a second application model. The same source content may be cloned multiple times into the same or different target model. No associations are maintained between related objects in the source and target models, therefore there is no capacity to update any cloned content in the target model.

The newly created objects in the target model are fully populated meaning they are persistently created in the context of the target model. The object type and category of the newly created objects will remain same in the target model. For example, a Design Component (Cpd0DesignElement) of category Shape from a source model is cloned into a target model, the category and the object type of the newly created object in the target model will still be the same as the object in the source model. Model elements when cloned across two different source models will be re-identified in the target model. For example, upon cloning new IDs will be assigned to the Design Component objects in the target model.

The elements to be included from the source to the target model can be either an explicit list of elements or results from a recipe. List of elements from the source model to be explicitly included (via multi-select action) can be passed to this operation for cloning the content into the target model.

Note: Internally BMIDE deep copy rules will be used to traverse and clone the source objects.


Preconditions:
1)    The source application model is with some pre-existing model content.
2)    Target application model already exists.
3)    Partitions (Member owns the membership) are pre created in target model if memberships are expected to be copied over to target model.


Cloning in the context of Partitions:

Note: Partitions are not cloned as part of this operation.

Application must leverage on Partition clone functionality to clone partition from one application model into another application model but the model content that resides in the source application model are cloned into the new application model using cloneModelContent Operation.

In order to create Partition breakdowns also in the target model, the applications must follow a two-step process.
1)    Perform Partition Template Clone using existing clonePartitions service operation to copy partitions from one model to another.
2)    Perform Template Clone with model content using the cloneModelContent service operation.

If the initial elements would reference partitions (member owned partitions) in the source application model, membership objects will be also be cloned if the target models have the same partitions else the model elements will be cloned as unassigned members. If same Partition memberships exist both in source model and target model then they are not recreated instead the existing memberships are retained.

Note:
1)    If the source model contains a reuse design component, then all its subordinate design components will be cloned. The system will warn and stop if the user is trying to clone only subordinate design component without its reuse design component.
2)    Delete on cloned content in the target model deletes the selected object alone. If the selected object to delete is a reuse Design Component, then all its subordinates will also be deleted.
3)    If the category of the newly created target object has to be different from source object types then it is Application's/Customer's responsibility to manage any such mappings through extension points provided by the infrastructure.


Note:

1) If the source model contain a reuse design component, then all its subordinate design components will be cloned. This is control by a business object contants called "cloneReuseAlongWithSubordinates". If the value of this constant is true, then reuse and its full chain of subordinates will be cloned togther, else reuse or the selected subordinate will be ignore.

2) Delete on cloned content in the target model deletes the selected object alone. If the selected object to delete is a reuse Design Component , then all its subordinates will also be deleted.

3) Variants and Effectivity conditions will not be carry forwarded onto the target objects in the target model by default alternatively this behavior can be controlled by a business object constant "cloneObjectsWithVariantExpr" , "cloneObjectsWithEffectivityExpr" . If the value of the contant is "true" then Variants or effectivity expressions will copied from source object.

Refer to TDOC for more information on prerequisites on Variant and effectivity expression carry over from source application model to target application model.

3) An error will be thrown if the source application model contains elements other than subtypes of Mdl0ConditionalModelElement.

Operation.useCase:
This operation supports the most common Clone Template use case for applications to re-use project work as part of their knowledge capture for future projects.

Templates shall be creatable in three different ways:
1)    An extract from an existing model.
2)    Authored from Scratch.
3)    Derived from another template (a.k.a. model). This derivation shall keep a relation to the original template.
From 4GD standpoint template is a specialization of an Application model which can contain explicit content, parameterized content and place holders.

Applications can clone the source template into target application model.. During clone operation, a configurable set of relationships will also be copied over from the selected elements to the new initial elements in the second application model. Once the cloning is completed the initial elements may be modified to fit better with the second application model's requirements.

Note: Re-cloning, revise and update on the source model content has no effect on the cloned content in the target model.

Operation.description:
This operation queries, filters, and configures all primary/secondary objects attached to the given input set of objects. Filter criteria are provided through the RelatedObjectInput construct. Filtering can be based on the type of the relation, the type of the related object, and relation attribute values. Configuration conditions are specified by a ConfigurationContext object, which provides revision and unit effectivity rule information. Returned objects are configured by the given configuration context and are access checked before being returned.

Some applications, such as CAD tools, need to navigate relationships and return results only if they match certain configuration criteria. An example is the navigation from a design component to a design control element. A design component may be related to multiple revisions of a design control element; however within a configured view of the system, only one of the design control elements may actually be relevant. This service operation helps find the secondary object (e.g. Cpd0DesignElement) of a relation (e.g. Cpd0ControlModel) given a primary object (e.g. Cpd0DesignControlElement).

RESTRICTION: Currently this operations support navigation of Mdl0CopyStableRelation and its subtypes only.

Operation.returnDescription: A set of objects that are access checked before being returned.

ParameterInfo.description: This vectors provides inputs of the objects for which related objects have to be queried along with query filters.

Operation.useCase:
This API supports the authoring use case where an object or a set of objects requires a new revision. Objects which are a subtype of Mdl0ConditionalElement support the concept of revise. The elements are first created by a user, undergo edits, and then are approved through a workflow and given status. At this point, a new revision of the object must be created to further modify it.
The reviseObjects operation is used to create the new revision. Deep copy rules, defined in BMIDE and deployed to Teamcenter, control the sub object copy process during the revise operation. The operation getReviseDesc is called prior to calling reviseObjects to construct the deep copy information and descriptors for the objects to be revised.
Use Case : Revise a conditional element
The following assumes an initial revision has been created and released.
    • Construct list of existing, released objects to be revised (objects must be valid subtypes of Mdl0ConditionalElement).
    • Construct deep copy data and get saveAs descriptors for the input set of objects by using operation getReviseDesc.
    • Revise the objects in Teamcenter by using the reviseObjects operation.
    • Post process / display new object revisions in client

Operation.description: This operation creates a geometric constraint collection containing model elements, i.e. foreground members (having their positions affected and possibly affecting other foreground members in the container) and background members (only affecting positions of foreground members). In addition, the CAD dataset specifying the geometric constraints among the members is also set.
Operation.exceptionCondition:
• 278701        Model Geometry internal error.
    • 278704        A model content object may only be a foreground member in a single geometric constraint collection. The newly requested foreground member must first be removed from its existing constraint container.
Operation.name: createCollection
Operation.returnDescription: The operation returns a list of CreatedConstraintCollection structures containing details for each collection created and the ServiceData. If there is any exception during an attempt to create a collection, the error will be added to the ServiceData object and returned as a partial error correlated by clientId.
Operation.useCase:
1.    Saving geometric constraint group data to Teamcenter by CAD.
This use case is entirely within the domain of CAD tools. Using this service operation a CAD tool will save the constraint collection data in Teamcenter. It will provide the model elements, i.e. foreground and background members and the CAD dataset specifying the geometric constraints among the members.

Example client to server interaction :
1)    A CAD tool calls createCollection passing in the initial set of desired members and provides their own generated csid values for each new member. ConstraintData will be populated with the desired Dataset type and desired named reference file type for the given CAD tool.
2)    The server returns a newly created collection, a newly created Dataset of the specified type, and also the ticketForNamedRef that was also created and associated to the new dataset. In the returned memberList for the new collection, the recorded csid values per member record are also returned.
3)    The CAD tool then uploads its constraint file using the returned ticketForNamedRef and saves the constraintDataSet.

Alternatively the server may be allowed to generate csids:
1)    A CAD tool calls createCollection passing in the initial set of desired members, but does not provide csid values for each new member. ConstraintData will be populated with the desired Dataset type and desired named reference file type for the given CAD tool.
2)    The server returns a newly created collection, a newly created dataset of the specified type, and also the ticketForNamedRef that was also created and associated to the new Dataset. In the returned memberList for the new collection, the newly allocated csid values per member record are also returned.
3)    The CAD tool takes the returned csid values for each new member and records them appropriately in its own CAD geometric constraint file. Then it uploads that file using the returned ticketForNamedRef and saves the constraintDataSet.

ParameterInfo.description: List of objects of <font face="courier" height="10">CreateCollectionInfo</font>. Each object contains the set of information needed to create the geometric constraint collection, its initial members and the initial constraint dataset.

If the mode is given as "configured", then the member content returned for a given container's saved-state will be modified (versus the precise member revisions) to consider an input configuration context to determine the revision (for members that support Revise operation ) that is returned as a member.

This operation calculates the effectivity for the given set of input objects. The effectivity calculation is done taking into account the precedence of other major revisions of the input objects.
